subject: Egress identity assertion + firewall fallback plan for private endpoint
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Alex Carter <alex@orchid-analytics.com>, secops@orchid-analytics.com
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Egress identity assertion + firewall fallback plan for private endpoint

Alex / Orchid SecOps —

Thanks for the detailed onboarding packet. Before we sign off on the private endpoint for Orchid Analytics, we need to close the egress identity and fallback behavior questions so your firewall team can complete the change window. High level asks:

1) Egress identity: Are you able to accept an asserted source identity token from our control plane when traffic exits the private connector? We can sign a short-lived JWT (kid + x5c) that includes: tenant_id, connector_id, ephemeral_ip, and timestamp. This token is presented over TCP (SNI header evidence) and logged in the TLS handshake.

2) Fallback behavior: If the outbound IP bound to your VPC is rotated or blackholed, our private connector can either (A) fail closed, (B) fail open to our hosted API with strict routing and audit logging, or (C) route through a customer-provided proxy. We need Orchid to confirm acceptable fallback mode and the associated ACLs.

3) Firewall rules: We propose a minimal set of destination FQDN/port pairs and a custody list of ephemeral egress ranges. The attached CSV has suggested CIDRs for connector egress; these are ephemeral for scale and will be updated with signed attestations.

4) Evidence and logging: For your SOC reviewers we can provide a zip of egress session logs with signed assertions and the corresponding public key material. Confirm the retention window and preferred format (syslog vs S3).

Action items for Orchid: please confirm (by EOD Monday) — which fallback mode you require, whether you can accept the JWT assertion approach, and the retention window. Our Security/Network teams (cc'd) are ready to supply test tokens and a small runbook for your firewall team to verify.

Thanks —
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: egress-assertion-runbook-v1.pdf (runbook, 6 pages)
Attachment: safelist-cidr-list.csv (proposed egress CIDRs)
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Alex Carter <alex@orchid-analytics.com>, secops@orchid-analytics.com
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 18:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Egress identity assertion + firewall fallback plan for private endpoint

Quick clarifications from infra:

- The JWT we plan to issue is short-lived (90s) and rotated per-connector. It will be presented as a custom TLS extension and mirrored in a request header we call X-RW-Egress-Assertion for HTTP flows. Non-HTTP flows will carry the token in a separate mTLS handshake metadata frame.

- Ephemeral IPs: we expect a stable pool for 24-48 hours by default, but they can move sooner during autoscaling events. We will publish a signed list each morning; we can also provide a push webhook to Orchid if they prefer real-time updates.

- If Orchid chooses 'fail open to hosted API', we will enforce a strict path with fallback logging + customer notification webhook; this mode is intended only for short incidents.

Laura
Sr. Product Manager, Redwood Console

On verification, we will provide a small curl + mtls sample and a Postman collection to replicate the token flow.
From: Alex Carter <alex@orchid-analytics.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: secops@orchid-analytics.com
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Egress identity assertion + firewall fallback plan for private endpoint

Hi team — thanks for the fast turnaround. SecOps reviewed this morning. Answers below: 

- JWT assertion: we can accept the signed JWT presented over TLS as described. Our firewall vendor (Palo Alto) can match on the SNI + a header fingerprint for HTTP. For non-HTTP flows, we will accept the mTLS metadata frame approach but need a schema for the metadata (field names and encoding).

- Fallback: Orchid requires default to 'fail closed' for the initial production window (first 30 days). We understand a temporary canary 'fail open' is available for emergency debug, but it must be approved by our on-call and be limited to 30 minutes and fully audited.

- Retention: provide logs in gziped JSONL format with at least 90 days retention. We prefer S3 push with a signed presigned URL per bundle.

Next steps: please send the mTLS metadata schema and a sample signed JWT. We will schedule a 45-minute firewall verification window (our side) on Tue 09/15 10:00 - 10:45 PT.

—Alex
Alex Carter, Head of SecOps, Orchid Analytics
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Alex Carter <alex@orchid-analytics.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: secops@orchid-analytics.com, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 08:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Egress identity assertion + firewall fallback plan for private endpoint

Thanks Alex — we'll prepare the artifacts. Quick note for the firewall window:

- I'll generate test tokens and a matching S3 bundle of signed evidence for the demo.
- The mTLS metadata schema will be attached as a small YAML excerpt in the runbook; it includes fields: tenant_id, connector_id, ephemeral_ip, issued_at, sig_alg, key_id. Encoding is base64url for the signature bytes.
- We'll also provide a transient IP pin for the hour of testing so you can lock down the rule to a single /32.

I'll upload the artifacts to the Drive link and ping the presigned URLs into this thread before Tue.

—Dylan
Platform Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Egress identity assertion + firewall fallback plan for private endpoint

All — good to hear. Final checklist I will bring to the Tue verification window: 

- Signed sample JWT (kid + x5c) and verification code snippet
- mTLS metadata schema (YAML) and Postman + curl samples for HTTP and raw TLS flows
- A single-hour transient /32 pin for your firewall rules (will be shared 30m before start)
- S3 presigned URL flow for 90-day JSONL bundles and a small example bundle for ingestion testing
- Runbook (egress-assertion-runbook-v1.pdf) describing failure modes and how to trigger 'hosted fallback' with audit hooks

If Orchid confirms 'fail closed' for production, we'll program the connector to be strict by default and only enable 'hosted fallback' via an emergency playbook WHO signs off (two-person approval).

See you Tue — attaching the runbook again for convenience.

Priyom
